comments.body:
Closing as a duplicate of 2c38-bef7-b045-4ecc, which was filed first, is in_progress, and already has a fix pushed as Gerrit change 1044 (commit f822315).

That ticket reached the same root cause independently and in more detail: changes 1031 (228b, c781127a2) and 1035 (7e77, 517e0470a) are individually green but semantically interact — the DET-floor short-circuit returns a BLOCK with zero finder calls, while test_plan_review_reuse fixtures assume the full review runs, because their plans carry no `## Acceptance Criteria` checklist and so never pass the deterministic floor.

Its chosen remedy is better than the one I proposed: fix the FIXTURES (give the test plans a DET-floor-passing AC shape) rather than touch production code, preserving each test intent. My write-up floated changing either side; theirs correctly identifies the tests as encoding a stale assumption.

Two things from my investigation worth carrying over, both recorded here rather than lost:

1. Gerrit rebased 1035 on submit and landed it WITHOUT re-running CI — its own message reads "Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 517e0470ab…". 1035s patchset was based on 36411da47, which predates c781127a2, so its green run (30524084670, 7659 passed) never saw the short-circuit. The combination was never gated. Worth considering whether a rebase-on-submit should re-verify.

2. Independently of the 228b interaction, these two tests are NOT self-contained: running their file alone fails identically at 1035s original pre-rebase patchset, at merged main, and on an unrelated branch (2 failed, 5 passed). They only pass inside a full-suite run, so they depend on state another test establishes. CI uses `pytest -n 4 --dist worksteal`, which distributes dynamically, so worker placement — and whether their unnamed dependency ran alongside — shifts whenever the suite changes. Even after 1044 lands, that latent fragility remains and can flip them red again when unrelated tests are added.

No further work needed on this ticket.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py::test_force_bypasses_verdict_reuse` and `::test_code_change_reruns_full_review` fail on `main`'s tree, blocking unrelated changes from earning `Verified +1`. Both assert `runner.calls > first_calls` and get `assert 0 > 0` — the fake LLM runner is never invoked at all.

Observed on Gerrit changes 1039 and 1040 (both `Verified -1`, both otherwise unrelated to plan review). Reproduces locally.

## Blame

**Primary: 228b-… (`c781127a2` "228b: short-circuit plan review on any DET block"), surfaced by a rebase-without-re-verify on 7e77-cbe5-5bcf-4096 (`517e0470a`, Gerrit change 1035).**

The two tests are built, per their own module docstring, on "a DET-floor BLOCK (missing Acceptance Criteria fails P1 unconditionally) with a schema-aware counting fake runner". They assert the LLM passes still RUN in that state. 228b changed exactly that contract — it short-circuits plan review on any DET block, so the runner is never called and `calls` stays 0.

The two changes never met in CI:
- 7e77's patchset was based on `36411da47` ("4143: remind about Serena…"), which PREDATES `c781127a2`. Its CI run 30524084670 was green (7659 passed) against that base — a base without the short-circuit.
- Gerrit then rebased it on submit. Its own message: "Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 517e0470ab…".
- The rebased commit was submitted WITHOUT re-running CI, so nothing ever tested 7e77's tests against 228b's behaviour.

This is the Rebase-If-Necessary semantic-conflict hazard: two changes each green in isolation, red once combined, with no gate on the combination.

## Confidence and what is NOT yet proven

Confirmed: the commit ordering, the two bases, the green CI on 7e77's pre-228b base, the rebase-on-submit message, and the failing assertions.

NOT confirmed: reverting only `c781127a2`'s `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py` on top of `517e0470a` did NOT restore green. So the short-circuit path as it exists on main is not solely that file — 7e77 also rewrote `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` (-52 lines) and added `reuse.py`, and the effective routing is likely the combination. Whoever picks this up should treat "228b's contract change vs 7e77's test assumption" as the lead, not as a finished diagnosis.

## Second, independent defect in the same tests

These tests are NOT self-contained. Run their file alone they fail identically — at 7e77's original pre-rebase patchset, at merged `main`, and on an unrelated feature branch:

    pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py    ->  2 failed, 5 passed

They only pass as part of a full-suite run, so they depend on state established by some other test. CI runs `pytest -n 4 --dist worksteal`, which distributes tests across workers DYNAMICALLY, so which worker they land on — and whether their unnamed dependency ran there — shifts whenever the suite changes. That makes them latently flaky regardless of the 228b conflict, and it is why adding unrelated tests can flip them red.

## Expected

1. Reconcile 228b's short-circuit contract with what 7e77's tests assert — either the tests encode a stale contract and should be updated, or the short-circuit is too aggressive for the `--force` / code-drift paths. That is a call for the owners of those two tickets, not a mechanical fix.
2. Make the two tests self-contained so they pass in isolation and cannot be flipped by worker distribution.
3. Consider whether Gerrit submitting a rebased commit without re-running CI needs a guard, since that is what let this land.

## Impact

`main`'s tree is failing these tests, so every unrelated change picking them up gets `Verified -1` and cannot land. Currently blocking Gerrit changes 1039 and 1040.
